name: Through-line mark
looks: One mark travels the whole film and changes form at every scene change: a dot becomes a band, the band a flood, a wipe, a sphere, a block, a button, a blob, and a dot again on the end card. Wherever one scene ends, the next scene picks the mark up from exactly that point, so the cuts read as one continuous move.
build: Choose the mark before writing any shots (an accent-coloured dot works for almost any film), and write what it means at each stop, not only where it sits; then write every shot's end state as the next shot's start state (its position, size and colour) so each seam is built before the scene between it.
sound: A recurring sound motif, one blip pitch, on the mark across every technique.
prompt: Choose one simple mark, such as a dot in the accent colour, and carry it through every scene of the film, having it change form and meaning at each stop: a node, an axis, a line, a button. Always end one scene exactly where the mark will begin the next, so every cut reads as one continuous move even as the technique underneath it changes completely.
source: the reel of 2026-10-06, whose angle was "One dot as the through-line: every scene starts from the last scene's mark (dot, band, circle, sphere, block, blue dot, button, blob), so the cuts read as one continuous move across eight techniques."
